description:
## What

New workspace crate `pkix-dane-resolver`. std-only. Provides:

- DNSSEC-validating resolver (likely built on hickory-dns / hickory-resolver with DNSSEC feature)
- API: `fn resolve_tlsa(host: &str, port: u16, proto: &str) -> Result<Vec<TlsaRecord>, ResolverError>`
- Async variant: `async fn resolve_tlsa_async(...)`
- Built-in TLSA cache respecting record TTLs
- Configurable upstream: system resolv.conf, hardcoded fallback, env override
- `Resolver` trait so consumers can plug their own implementation

## Depends on

- PKIX-j32w.1 (pkix-dane TLSA types)
- Decision PKIX-j32w.5 (DNS config source)

## Open shape decisions

- Sync wrapper over async hickory: spawn_blocking + ad-hoc runtime, or expose async only and require consumers to provide a runtime?
- Cache strategy: in-memory only, or admit on-disk cache via trait?
- Hickory feature set: minimum needed for DNSSEC. Hickory's full feature set is large.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Resolver trait + default hickory-backed impl
- [ ] DNSSEC validation (signed responses required; unsigned = treated as DNSSEC-fail per failure-mode policy in .4)
- [ ] In-memory TLSA cache with TTL respect
- [ ] System resolv.conf as default upstream
- [ ] Test against a public DANE-deployed name (e.g., dnssec-tools.org) as a smoke test; offline tests use captured responses
- [ ] ResolverError satisfies non-negotiable #6 (Clone+Debug+PartialEq+Eq+Send+Sync; serde behind feature flag)

## Stub status

Future work. Filed as architectural commitment under PKIX-j32w.
